opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin to Payroll. As full-time employee, max is write unless their role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll, so admin is not allowed. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E022 (Timothy Wallace) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Requested admin to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Engineer (max write), while Security DB states contractor with basic security training (max read). Admin is not permitted under either reading (Engineer does not own Payroll; contractors never get admin). Given the conflicting facts and the principle of least privilege, I grant the more conservative maximum: read.
